prime.problem: The distribution of a total (claims over two weeks) is not the sum of the two pmfs, and doubling one week is also wrong. You need every way the total can split between the independent parts.
prime.fits: The third conditioning card: condition on how much of the total the first week takes. Its generating-function view is the tool that the MGF card, the negative binomial (a sum of geometrics) and the Poisson (rates add) all reuse.
expect: the sum over splits, P(X = k) P(Y = s − k)
the anti-diagonal of the joint grid
PGFs: the generating function of a sum is the product
prime.goal: Compute the pmf of a sum of independent counts, both by the convolution sum and by multiplying generating functions.

attend: Why is every split of 7 claims equally likely here (1/512 each), and would that survive a different pmf?
Why is 2N always even, and what does that say about 'two weeks = one week doubled'?
How does multiplying two power series do the split-and-sum for every total at once?
Why does the normal approximation come out 41% too low here?

must: Total s of independent X and Y → condition on X = k → then Y must be s − k → P(S = s) = Σ P(X = k) P(Y = s − k), s + 1 terms

Write a pmf as Σ P(N = n) zⁿ → multiplying two series collects the exponent pairs that add to s → G<sub>S</sub> = G<sub>X</sub>G<sub>Y</sub> = 1/(2 − z)² → P(S = s) = (s + 1)/2<sup>s+2</sup> for every s
Independence is what makes the joint a product → if a bad week makes the next one worse, the product rule fails → you must sum the joint table's diagonal instead
elevated: np.convolve does all totals in O(nm), and an FFT does it in O(n log n) → that matters for long pmfs, not for a single total

compress.prompt: From memory, draw the 8-by-8 grid of (week 1, week 2) outcomes, shade the cells that total 7, and write in 3 sentences why their sum is P(S = 7) and why each cell is 1/512.
checklist: the cells on one anti-diagonal are the splits of the total
each cell is P(X = k) × P(Y = s − k), a product because the weeks are independent
here the exponents always add to 9, so every split is 1/512
the generating function does all totals at once: (s + 1)/2<sup>s+2</sup>
the sum is NB(2, ½), with mean 2 and variance 4

retrieve.q: Explain why P(N<sub>1</sub> = 7) + P(N<sub>2</sub> = 7) is not P(N<sub>1</sub> + N<sub>2</sub> = 7).
answer: the sum of the pmfs answers 'did either week alone hit 7?' (and isn't even that exactly)
you need every split, each weighted by the product of the two probabilities

retrieve.q: Trace P(S = 3) by the convolution sum and check it against (s + 1)/2<sup>s+2</sup>.
Convolution sum, generating function or normal approximation: which for (a) one total of two counts, (b) a sum of 50 i.i.d. counts, (c) the full pmf of a long sum on a computer?
answer: (a) the convolution sum: s + 1 exact products
(b) raise the generating function or MGF to the 50th power, or use the CLT if you only need an approximation
(c) np.convolve, or an FFT for very long pmfs
the normal approximation fails for two skewed terms: 0.00924 against the exact 1/64

compare.q: Adding independent Poissons against adding these geometric weeks: both families are closed under addition. How does the generating function show each, and what would break it?
answer: Poisson: e<sup>λ(z−1)</sup> multiplies by adding the exponents, so the rates add
the weeks: 1/(2 − z) squared is the NB(2, ½) generating function
dependence between the parts breaks both: the joint is no longer a product

compare.q: Exact convolution against the CLT's normal approximation: what does each assume, and when does the approximation become safe?
answer: convolution is exact for any independent summands and any number of terms
the CLT needs many i.i.d. terms with finite variance
with two skewed terms it misses by 41% (0.00924 against 0.015625); with many terms the skew averages out

predict.q: The two weeks had 7 claims in total. What is P(week 1 had exactly 3)? Commit first.
predict.answer: 1/8. Every one of the 8 splits had the same joint probability, 1/512, so given the total they stay equally likely: P(N<sub>1</sub> = 3 | S = 7) = (1/512)/(1/64) = 1/8. That is Bayes applied to the convolution's cases, and the uniform answer is special to this pmf.

apply.task: Three weeks: G<sub>S</sub> = 1/(2 − z)³. Get P(S = 7) two ways: a double sum over (k<sub>1</sub>, k<sub>2</sub>) with Fractions, and the coefficient of z⁷, using 1/(1 − x)³ = Σ C(s + 2, 2) xˢ.
apply.hint: Factor out ½ from each week: 1/(2 − z)³ = (1/8) × 1/(1 − z/2)³.
